summary: The operator's view, everything at once: who holds the card now (`rental`) and every process its rental put on the card - each one's pid, the proof its command line carries, its model, engine, port, memory (`mib`, null when not measured) and since when the coordinator has known of it - every ticket in line - waiting or offered, in the order the card will be offered, each with its class and since when, and scheduled work's time it starts no earlier than (`not_before`) and, waiting for room, the numbers it waits on (`room`) - which ports are held and by whom, and since when the coordinator has been running - a holder that sees `started_at` move knows the coordinator restarted and rebuilt its state. A rental is `held`; `releasing` while its release is checked; `reclaiming` while a lapsed rental's processes are ended on proof - and the card goes to no one else until that is done. This is the operator's route, not an application's: no answer to an application names another, and a server asking whether the coordinator is up asks `/up`. `actor` is the coordinator's own id, minted when it started; `contract_version` the version of the contract it runs (`contract_version()` in the contract's validate.py), as a server's health carries its own. `limits` are the coordinator's settings: a rental's lifetime between heartbeats (`ttl_s`), the claim window once the card is offered (`claim_s`), how long a waiting ticket nobody waits on is kept (`drop_s`), the longest a wait is held open (`hold_s`), how long a release waits for the rental's processes to go and the card's memory to come back before it ends what is left on proof (`settle_s`), the free memory kept beside what a ticket or an amend needs (`margin_mib`), how long an amend right after one of the rental's own processes went waits for its memory to come back (`amend_settle_s`), and how often the card is read again for scheduled work waiting for room (`recheck_s`). `port_range` is where the ports it hands out come from. `card` is the card as the machine sees it - how much of its memory is in use - or `known: false` when it cannot be asked; the page shows it, and a grant and an amend each read the card afresh for themselves. `lock` is the machine's card lock (the contract's `machine/card-lock.json`): `held` - this coordinator is the way onto the card, and its note gives its address; `waiting` - an application run on its own has the card, and no ticket is offered it until the lock is this coordinator's (`detail` says who holds it: the operator's page names everyone; a note beside the lock whose writer has gone is stale: it names nobody, and `detail` says it is stale, and what it claimed); `none` - a coordinator built in code, holding no lock. No token is ever in it. THE WATCH (PLAN-4 D3): `limits` also says how long a rental that says it is working may go without its progress moving before it is taken back (`hang_s`), how often the card is read during a rental (`watch_s`), the free memory under which a rental is degraded (`floor_mib`), and the free memory under which the card counts as full - an answer far slower than its model's normal, said by a heartbeat, then marks the rental degraded too (`full_mib`) - and, while a rental is degraded, how often the card is read instead, so a card with room again is noticed within seconds (`recover_watch_s`): it clears on the first read with room for what the rental needs - the need of its models, less what its processes hold now, plus the floor - never merely over the floor. `watch` is what the coordinator knows of the rental's work, from its heartbeats - whether it says it is working, its progress, when that last moved, a one-piece answer's deadline (`due_at`) - and when the card was last read for it (`read_at`), and how many of its answers its heartbeats counted far slower than their model's normal since the grant (`slow_answers`, the count the last heartbeat said - on a card with room they are only counted, and this is where the count is seen); null with no rental. `card.ours_mib` is what the rental's processes use - each one's measured `mib`, or else the need its model was approved with: an estimate - 0 with no rental, null when one of them has neither; `card.outside_mib` is the rest of the card's use, outside the bootstrap: `used_mib - ours_mib`, never below 0, null when either is not known.
